title: GitLab week 4 review - testing the XYZ application
description: Eight questions on CI for a real app: install, tests, reports, coverage and advisory jobs.

questions.prompt: npm ci fails: package.json and package-lock.json are out of sync. Whose problem is it?

options.text: The application's - the lock was not updated; CI caught it

questions.explanation: A reproducible install exposed a real mistake before review.

questions.prompt: Which artifacts key turns test results into a merge request widget?
questions.explanation: reports:junit is parsed into the Test summary and the Tests tab.

questions.prompt: Why must the test report artifact use when: always?

options.text: Because the report matters most when tests fail, and on_success would drop it

questions.explanation: Default on_success throws away exactly the failing run's report.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between the coverage: regex and a coverage_report artifact?

options.text: The regex gives a single percentage from the log; coverage_report gives line-level coverage in the MR diff
The regex is per line, the report is per job

questions.explanation: Use both: a number for the badge and widget, Cobertura for the diff.

questions.prompt: A job with allow_failure: true fails. What colour is the pipeline and do later stages run?
How do you let a linter's findings be advisory but still fail when the linter itself crashes?
questions.explanation: ESLint exits 1 for problems and 2+ for errors; allow only the former.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with 'npm test; echo done' as the last line of a script?

options.text: The echo's exit code becomes the job's, hiding a test failure
echo is not available in alpine

questions.explanation: The last command decides the job status.

questions.prompt: Why are integration tests a separate job from unit tests?

options.text: They need a service and take longer; separate jobs run in parallel and keep unit tests fast
GitLab allows only one test job

questions.explanation: Same stage, parallel, each failing independently.
